title: Mashbooh
subtitle: Ingredient of uncertain origin under Islamic Law.
what_body: BOTIA signals when the halal or haram status cannot be confirmed from the label alone.
why_body: Under Islamic Law, an ingredient derived from an unlawful source is also unlawful (Codex CAC/GL 24-1997). However, food labels worldwide are not required to declare where many ingredients actually come from. Flavourings, emulsifiers, enzymes, gelatines and glycerol can all be animal, plant or alcohol-based, and the label looks exactly the same either way.
can_1: Detect ingredients whose origin is left undeclared on the label.
can_2: Explain why that specific ingredient can be animal, plant or alcohol-based.
can_3: Make the silence visible, so the decision is yours and not the manufacturer's by omission.
cannot_1: Confirm or deny halal status — it is not a certification body.
cannot_2: Know the real origin of an ingredient the label never declared.
cannot_3: Replace a certified halal authority or your own religious judgement.
closing: The origin was not declared. That is not a verdict — it is the information you were missing.
